title: Client compatibility shims for telemetry schema evolution
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Console backend and our ingestion pipeline are moving to a structured analytics schema (v2) to support richer event types and definitive typing. Several clients (JS/Go SDKs, CLI tool) still emit v1-shaped payloads. Goal: implement a low-risk, observable migration path that preserves customer telemetry and enables server-side schema upgrades without breaking client integrations.

Proposed approach: 1) Introduce lightweight client-side compatibility shims bundled into SDKs and the CLI that can operate in two modes: pass-through (no change) and mapped (translate v1 -> v2). 2) Use explicit protocol negotiation: clients send Accept-Schema: v1,v2 and servers respond with X-Server-Schema: v2 (or v1) and optional X-Mapping-Hint header. 3) Add a runtime compatibility adapter on the ingest edge that understands both v1 and v2 and emits a canonical internal format while attaching schema_version metadata. 4) Provide a mapping table repository (versioned JSON) in S3 and surfaced in Console for manual overrides. 5) Ship a compatibility test harness in CI that runs every SDK/CLI change against the server's ingest compatibility layer for the matrix of schema versions. 6) Rollout plan: enable ingest adapter to accept v1 and v2 in all regions -> deploy shims in SDKs and CLI behind a feature flag -> enable mapped translations for 5% of traffic (canary) -> monitor regressions for 2 weeks -> incrementally increase to 100% and deprecate v1 after 90 days with deprecation notice.

Why client shims: allows teams to opt-in at their cadence, reduces server parsing pressure during migration, and provides better developer ergonomics for customers who cannot upgrade immediately.

Telemetry & monitoring: capture metrics for "telemetry.schema.mismatch", "telemetry.translation.errors", and token-level size deltas via existing ingestion metrics. Add a dashboard showing per-customer mismatch rate and downstream eval diffs. Create alerts for translation error rate > 0.5% or if mapped payloads increase median processing latency > 15ms.

Security and privacy: shims only transform field names and structure; no PII extraction. Ensure schema mapping repo access is access-controlled (KMS keys) and audit-logged.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field for discrete checks.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs and CLI include an opt-in compatibility shim that can map v1 events to v2 shape
Server responds with X-Server-Schema and logs incoming schema version for each event
Compatibility adapter in ingest handles mixed-version traffic without data loss for 30k events/min
CI matrix runs compatibility tests covering SDK v1->server v2 and SDK v2->server v1
Dashboard shows per-customer schema mismatch rate and translation error trends
Canary rollout configured by customer hash and can be paused/rolled back via Console
